# A Saturday at the repair library

We arrived early because the first bus was usually crowded. The caretaker had already opened the side door, and sunlight reached all the way across the empty tables. Outside, someone was unloading a bicycle with a broken basket. Nobody seemed to know who had booked it in, so we made tea while the owner searched for the confirmation on her phone.

The small box of tools were waiting beside the window. I carried it to the nearest table and checked the list against the contents. A screwdriver was missing, but there were two spare handles and enough tape to finish the first repair. Maya said she had saw the missing tool in the cupboard on Friday. We looked there together and found it behind a stack of old magazines.

By ten o’clock the room was full. A volunteer explained the booking system to a visitor who had never used a computer. Another showed a child how to thread a needle. The instructions were deliberately short: find the loose seam, choose a matching thread, and work slowly. Their patience made the place feel welcoming.

I recieved a message from the baker across the street just before lunch. He had saved yesterday’s rolls for us and wanted someone to collect them. We took two bags and left the coins in the jar by his till. On the way back, rain began to fall, first in scattered drops and then in a steady sheet.

When the last visitor left, we swept the floor and wrote down the repairs that still needed parts. The bicycle basket was secure, the radio played again, and the child took home a neatly mended bag. I was tired, but I was glad we had kept the doors open.
